title: Cloak and Dagger
paragraphs: A wartime espionage anthology dramatizing dangerous intelligence missions and resistance work, drawing its atmosphere and subject matter from accounts of Allied clandestine operations.

NBC sustaining wartime-espionage anthology dramatizing OSS missions, based on the 1946 book Cloak and Dagger: The Secret Story of the OSS by Corey Ford and Alistair MacBain. The frozen set contains all 22 documented broadcast programs; no historical program is missing.

The run breaks into several distinct periods: Sunday 4 PM period (May 7, 1950 to August 27, 1950) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]], Friday 8 PM period (September 1, 1950 to October 6, 1950) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]], and Final Sunday broadcasts (October 15, 1950 to October 22, 1950) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]].

Names that turn up again and again in the surviving run include Sherman Marks (director), Louis G. Cowan (producer and director), Corey Ford (creator, performer, and author), Alfred Hollander (producer, performer, and director), Alistair MacBain (creator and performer), Jon Gart (music director and music), and [[person|raymond-edward-johnson|Raymond Edward Johnson]] (performer).
Across its run, the surviving broadcasts are tied to [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]].

The stories often return to Office of Strategic Services clandestine operations, espionage, sabotage and intelligence work, World War II occupied territories, postwar dramatization of wartime intelligence, resistance networks and partisan support, and cover identities, deception and counterintelligence.

The show also sits in a wider radio history that includes Korean War bulletin preceding The Eyes of Buddha, OSS wartime clandestine operations, 1946 Cloak and Dagger source book, and NBC sustaining espionage series.

If you are following the same actors and creative circles, related programs worth opening next include [[show|x-minus-one|X Minus One]], [[show|columbia-workshop|Columbia Workshop]], [[show|words-at-war|Words at War]], [[show|cbs-radio-mystery-theater|CBS Radio Mystery Theater]], and [[show|the-chase|The Chase]].
